overview: This Senate resolution designates September 9, 2025, as "National World War II Italian Campaign Remembrance Day," marking the date in 1943 when American forces landed at Salerno to begin freeing mainland Italy from German occupation. It recounts the 602-day campaign, including the invasion of Sicily, the battles of Monte Cassino and Anzio, and the liberation of Rome in June 1944, and notes the roughly 150,000 American casualties. The resolution honors American and Allied troops, supports preserving battlefields and cemeteries in Italy, and encourages Americans to mark the day with ceremonies and education while few veterans of the campaign remain. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on October 6, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution preserves the memory of a long, costly campaign and honors the sacrifice of those who served before living memory fades.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
